target_customer: Employers (UK-based clients such as NHS, Defra, Benefex per its site) buying reproductive and hormone health benefits for staff
problem: Employee health coverage leaves gaps in fertility, menopause, endometriosis/PCOS, men's and trans/non-binary health care.
business_model: B2B employer benefit sold per employer (pricing not found)
product_category: Women's and reproductive health employee benefit / virtual care

founders.name: Anya Roy
founders.background_notes: Cambridge bioscience (Christ's College) per YC page; masters in bioscience entrepreneurship per interview summary; venture capital and genomics experience.

founders.name: Chantelle Bell
founders.background_notes: Classmate of Roy at Cambridge masters; not listed on YC page.

competitors.name: Peppy
competitors.what: B2B menopause and fertility support platform for employers (UK)

competitors.name: Carrot Fertility
competitors.funding_then: Series B 24M USD in 2020-08, total about 40M USD

technical_complexity.rationale: Employer benefit packaging, virtual consults and at-home tests mostly rely on partners; the original diagnostic device idea was harder but the current product does not appear to need it.

defensibility.rationale: Employer contracts create some stickiness but well-funded benefit platforms covered the same needs; no proprietary data evidenced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Carrot later added menopause and low-testosterone benefits (Fierce Healthcare, date not retrieved), moving toward Syrona's inclusive scope; no acquisition of Syrona found.

market_need_then: Syrona cites 30B USD of out-of-pocket costs for treatments poorly covered by insurance (company claim). Investor appetite for employer fertility and menopause benefits shown by Peppy and Carrot rounds in 2020-2021.

identity.voice_and_tone: Inclusive, supportive: 'Healthcare isn't one-size-fits-all' and 'Empower Your People' on the site.

rebrands.why: Not stated; early coverage 2018-2020 used Syrona Women and the YC listing uses Syrona Health, reflecting broadened scope

brand_strength.rationale: Name is distinctive but no source on brand impact or origin; companion app is called Sora.

pivots.from: Diagnostic device for early detection of cervical cancer and gynaecological disease (Syrona Women, 2018 coverage)
pivots.to: Employer benefit and virtual care platform
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; a podcast index mentions a pivot from medical device to healthcare platform

outcome_analysis: Syrona Health is still active per YC and its site, serving UK employers including NHS and Defra by its own testimonials, after pivoting from a diagnostic device to an employer benefit. No verified funding rounds beyond a Cambridge-listed total of 2.6M GBP were found, so whether it succeeded, stalled or is simply small cannot be judged from public sources.
notes: Funding unverified: Cambridge JBS page lists 2.6M GBP total raised (undated); aggregators give 0.5M to 2M USD with conflicting dates (2019, 2022); no round recorded. No outcome news found (no shutdown or acquisition); team size 6 per YC. Founders-for-Good podcast may explain pivot and name but was not fetched. Competitor traction not retrieved. Web Archive skipped. Completeness pass: two rounds are recorded from Seedtable alone (pre-seed 500K in 2022-01 and a 0.25M seed dated 2019). Totals elsewhere conflict (CB Insights 740K over 12 rounds, Caplight 1.08M, Village 2M, Tracxn 575K, Cambridge JBS 2.6M GBP), so the recorded rounds are partial and may not be complete. Investors not recorded because only aggregators name them.
